source.title: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation
source.authors: Ji-Ke Zhong; Ming Li; Yu-Xiang Lai; Xi Xiao; Sheng-Xuan Zhang; Ritwick Chaudhry; Tian-Le Chen; Jing-Yu Xie; Zheda Mai; Shao-Yuan Lo; Konstantinos Psounis; Yuan-Yuan Lei

page_placements.theme: Training dynamics: early student gains, then regression as the student fits supervisor errors or over-optimises the teacher's signal

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables and figures are flattened, but the reported main results are assignable; no missing section is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Extends the related question of students exceeding teachers to multi-turn agentic on-policy distillation. However, it studies smaller students distilled from stronger teachers, the reverse of the weak-supervisor/strong-student setup in the claim.
record.gate_note: The study does not test strong students trained on labels from weaker supervisors or report PGR. Its measured student-versus-teacher results concern the inverse size and supervision relationship, so the rows are recorded under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study distils smaller students (Qwen3.5-2B, Gemma-4-E4B) from larger, stronger teachers (27B, 31B) by on-policy distillation on agentic tasks. This is the reverse of the claim's setup, where a strong student learns from a weaker supervisor's labels. It reports no PGR and no strong ceiling. Burns et al. appears only in related work, as one route to students exceeding teachers. The 'student beats teacher' overshoot is a related but different construct, so it belongs under fits_no_version, not a test of V1–V6. The reader's 'tests/T3' is wrong.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors identify 'distillation overshoot' in agentic OPD: smaller students surpass larger teachers mid-training, then regress. They attribute this to repair of weak decisions outpacing, then being overtaken by, erosion of successful teacher-disfavored choices. SPOD (masking plus a soft floor) preserves and extends these gains in all six settings.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses on-policy distillation from a stronger, larger teacher to a smaller student on multi-turn agentic tasks; it does not use the weak-supervisor/strong-student weak-to-strong recipe or calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model family and benchmark; the paper reports peaks followed by declines as ordinary OPD training continues. It reports 3 training seeds for ordinary OPD and 3 evaluation seeds per checkpoint.

fits_no_version.finding: In multi-turn agentic on-policy distillation, smaller students distilled from larger teachers exceed teacher success mid-training, then regress (ALFWorld: Qwen peak 86.1% vs teacher 80.0%, final 80.7%; Gemma peak 82.8% vs 68.9%, final 73.7%). Final results vary by benchmark. The pattern also appears under reverse KL (Table 7: peak 84.7%, final 82.5%) and in 9 of 11 runs across OPD methods (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Students distilled on-policy from stronger teachers can transiently surpass teacher task success, because repair of weak decisions initially outpaces erosion of the student's own successful choices.

record.problems: The authors report three training seeds for ordinary OPD and three evaluation seeds per checkpoint but provide no uncertainty values in the cited main results. Their stated scope is two teacher–student pairs and three text-based agentic benchmarks; several comparison methods use one training seed each.
record.rows_left_out: SPOD results, its ablations, and comparisons with alternative OPD methods are omitted because they evaluate the paper’s proposed method rather than the weak-to-strong claim. Decision-level erosion analyses and task-group analyses are also omitted from rows because they do not measure a version of the claim.

untested.parts: No strong student trained on a weaker supervisor's labels; no PGR. Here the supervisor is larger and stronger.
SPOD is an OPD loss change aimed at teacher-surpassing gains. It is not evaluated as a PGR gain over naive weak-to-strong fine-tuning.
No weak-to-strong sweep over supervisor or student size, task, or representation.
No tests of weak-to-strong failure modes (exploitation, distribution shift, correlated errors).
The stylized two-decision model (Prop. 3.1) covers transient overshoot under forward-KL imitation of a stronger teacher. It gives no conditions for beating a weaker supervisor.
Text-based agentic benchmarks only; no vision.

record.verdict_notes: Despite the 'student beats teacher' framing, this is strong-to-weak distillation and does not bear on the weak-to-strong versions. Uncertainty is not shown in the main tables. The comparison baselines (TCOD, Guided-OPD, SAGE-OPD) use one training seed each.

versions.untested_parts: No strong student trained on a weaker supervisor’s labels; no PGR reported.
SPOD changes OPD training, but the study does not test the listed weak-to-strong method gains or compare PGR.
No weak-to-strong PGR sweep by student or supervisor size, task, or representation. The tested models and agentic tasks use stronger teachers and smaller students.
Does not test the listed weak-to-strong failure modes.
Its theory concerns overshoot in a stylized on-policy distillation setup, not conditions for a student to beat a weaker supervisor.
The study evaluates text-based agentic benchmarks, not vision.

relation.reason: Related work cites Burns et al. as a separate route to students surpassing teachers; the study's experiments concern stronger-teacher on-policy distillation.

tranche.reason: The experiments train smaller, initially weaker students from stronger teachers. They neither test nor use the catalog's weaker-supervisor/stronger-student finding.

source_check.notes: The numerical results and authors-conclusion paraphrase are supported. States above assess weak_to_strong claim versions; the reported gains and regressions remain valid observations of distillation overshoot.
